summary: Frontend-only verification of the bilingual EN/ES refactor of the two public no-login demos (/demo DemoFlow and /demo-all DemoAll) plus the LanguageSuggestBanner. Tested via REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL with localStorage 'unitech_lang' and 'unitech_lang_dismiss' set BEFORE reload. RESULT: All acceptance criteria met. ZERO Spanish words and ZERO 'translate from Spanish' references found anywhere in the app UI when unitech_lang='en' on either route, including all 3 /demo-all branches (Negocio / Presencia / Marketing). Spanish mode shows the expected ES copy (lead H1s, describe step, branch selector). The suggestion banner renders with correct data-testids, switches the whole UI to Spanish on click, and disappears (writes unitech_lang='es' + unitech_lang_dismiss='1' to localStorage).

issues: The EMAIL input placeholder is 'tu@email.com' (Spanish 'tu' = 'your') even when unitech_lang='en'. All other lead-form labels/buttons are correctly English. Consider switching the placeholder to 'you@email.com' for the English locale. Same placeholder appears on /demo-all lead in EN mode.

The bottom-right corner badge baked into the generated social post graphic shows 'IA' (Spanish for AI) instead of 'AI' when locale is English. This is part of the rendered post image, not surrounding UI. Confirm whether the watermark should be locale-aware; left as-is by main agent.

A small 'ES' chip appears inside the mini-site phone preview (top-right of the device frame). This is the mini-site's own language selector (in-product preview), not app chrome, so it is acceptable. Flagging only for awareness.

action_items: OPTIONAL: change the email input placeholder from 'tu@email.com' to 'you@email.com' when i18n locale is 'en' (DemoFlow.js and DemoAll.js lead forms).
OPTIONAL: consider making the 'IA' watermark on the generated marketing post template locale-aware ('AI' for EN).
critical_code_review_comments: EN/ES copy parity for /demo and /demo-all is clean. No raw i18n keys leaked; namespaces demo / demoFlow / demoAll resolve in both languages.

data-testids are present and correct for all critical actions: demo-name, demo-email, demo-trade, demo-start-btn, demo-example-roof, demo-gen-quote-btn, demo-accept-quote-btn, demo-sign-btn, demo-pay-btn, demo-all-name, demo-all-email, demo-all-start-btn, select-negocio-branch, select-presencia-branch, select-marketing-branch, demo-all-example-0, demo-all-gen-quote-btn, demo-nfc-tap, demo-mkt-example-0, demo-mkt-generate-btn, lang-suggest-banner, lang-suggest-switch-es.
Banner correctly persists dismissal via unitech_lang_dismiss='1' and language via unitech_lang in localStorage; reading happens before mount so no FOUC observed.
seed_data_creation: None (used demo lead names 'John Smith' / 'Jane Doe' / 'Pedro García', all transient, no persistence)

Banner: with unitech_lang='en' and dismiss removed, lang-suggest-banner renders text '¿Hablas español? Mira UniTech en tu idioma.' with button 'Ver en español' (data-testid='lang-suggest-switch-es'); clicking switches UI to Spanish, hides banner, sets unitech_lang='es' and unitech_lang_dismiss='1'. Only minor copy nits are the 'tu@email.com' placeholder and 'IA' watermark on marketing post (see design_issues).
